body:
**Type:** Bug · **Priority:** P0

## Problem and current evidence

On 2026-11-10 the Formal AI session for a Rust test repository posted this in its working session summary ([comment](https://github.com/konard/test-hello-world-019fb331-c107-78c7-8ff6-9f127a3c593c/pull/2#issuecomment-6763525155), 09:13:41Z):

> Learned standing requirement (you): You are an AI issue solver using `@link-assistant/agent`. …

The text after "(you):" is the complete system prompt of **another** session: it names the branch `issue-1-1f3e3886bcb8` and the repository of the Scala test (`konard/test-hello-world-019fb330-00e1-73b9-955e-f357a1600d5b`). The Rust pull request works on branch `issue-1-09b0c76bd0e4` in a different repository. The same block is repeated in six summaries of that pull request (comments 6763525155, 6763561282, 6763596673, 6763631221, 6763668006, 6763701940).

Consequences: instructions of one task (branch to push to, repository, issue number) are presented to another task as a rule it should follow; the summary grows by a full prompt on every turn; text of one repository's session is published in another repository.

Mechanism, read in the source at `70935ad8e`:

1. Dreaming lifts a "requirement" from any event that is not from the assistant or the system and whose content contains a cue such as "always", "never", "must", "should", "make sure", "do not" ([dreaming-cues.lino](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/70935ad8e2a12bc2148eef74722749290c2edb66/data/meta/dreaming-cues.lino); `requirement_statement` in `rust/src/dreaming/learning.rs`, JS twin [dreaming-learning.mjs](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/70935ad8e2a12bc2148eef74722749290c2edb66/js/server/dreaming-learning.mjs#L65-L72)). The whole content becomes the rule. A solver prompt of several thousand characters contains these words many times.
2. The topic of the event is its first significant word ([`eventTopic`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/70935ad8e2a12bc2148eef74722749290c2edb66/js/server/dreaming-learning.mjs#L41-L53)). For a prompt that begins "You are an AI issue solver" the topic is `you`.
3. A stored `meta_algorithm_amendment` is appended to every later answer whose prompt contains the topic as a token ([`topicMatches`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/70935ad8e2a12bc2148eef74722749290c2edb66/js/server/standing-requirements.mjs#L63-L71), [`applyRetainedAmendments`](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/70935ad8e2a12bc2148eef74722749290c2edb66/js/server/standing-requirements.mjs#L96-L98); message text in [server-messages.lino](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/70935ad8e2a12bc2148eef74722749290c2edb66/data/meta/server-messages.lino#L174)). The token "you" is in almost every prompt.

Not traced yet: why the memory of the first session was visible to the second one (the two runs used different client tools on the same host), and which step ran dreaming between them.

## Outcome that unblocks development

A prompt that configures one session is never stored as a standing requirement. What Formal AI learns from one task reaches another task only as a generalized rule with a scope, never as the text of the earlier request.

## Implementation steps

1. Do not learn requirements from system or developer instructions, however the client delivers them (many clients send them as the first user message); mark the role when the request is received.
2. Bound a learned rule: one statement, not a whole message; reject a rule above a size limit or one that contains identifiers of a single task (repository, branch, issue or pull request number, path of a working directory).
3. Derive the topic from the subject of the statement; pronouns and other function words are not topics in any supported language.
4. Scope every amendment (repository, user, conversation) and apply it only inside that scope unless it was generalized and verified by replay.
5. Do not append amendments to a final answer that is published outside the conversation; list them in the trace.
6. Trace why two sessions shared memory on the Hive Mind host and isolate the stores per session unless sharing is requested.
7. Add tests in both runtimes: a solver prompt followed by a second session in another repository yields no amendment text in the second answer.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Replaying the two recorded prompts in order produces a second summary with no text of the first prompt.
- [ ] No stored amendment has a pronoun as its topic.
- [ ] No stored rule is longer than the configured limit or contains a branch or repository name of one task.
- [ ] A real standing requirement stated by a user ("always answer in Russian") is still learned and applied in that user's later conversations.

## Dependency contract

**Blocked by:** none; this step can start independently.

**Blocks:** none declared in this plan.

Related umbrella issues provide context; their entire broader scope is not an implicit prerequisite.

This issue was created with `no-formal-ai-draft` so that opening the planning issues of #1548 together did not start a draft build for each. When it is selected, remove that label and explicitly dispatch `Hive Mind draft` for it.
title: [Bug][P0] A system prompt of one session is stored as a learned standing requirement and replayed in the summary of another repository's session
